faq.anonymousQ: Will my employer know I wrote a review?
faq.anonymousA: No. Only your chosen display name is shown. Employers never see who wrote a review, and reviews from small workplaces are published with a random delay.
faq.verifiedA: The reviewer showed a payslip or contract, came through the employer's invite, or applied through RateThatJob. Verified reviews count more in the score.
faq.employerA: No. Employers can reply and dispute unverified reviews, but they can't delete, hide or buy reviews.
faq.freeA: No. Reading, reviewing and applying are free for workers.

faq.removeQ: Can we remove a negative review?
faq.removeA: No, and nobody can buy their way out. You can reply publicly, and dispute unverified reviews that break the rules.
faq.anonymousQ: Can we see who wrote a review?
faq.anonymousA: No. Anonymity is what makes reviews honest. You see replies, trends and aggregate numbers from 5 reviews.
faq.disputeQ: What happens when we dispute a review?
faq.disputeA: Our team checks it against the rules. Reviews that break them are removed; honest criticism stays.
faq.costA: Claiming and the basic features are free. Pro is billed per location, monthly or yearly with 2 months free.

About.title: Know before you go.
About.intro: RateThatJob shows what it is really like to work at restaurants, shops, warehouses and factories – location by location, from the people who worked there.

principles.anonymousBody: Employers never learn who wrote a review or who answered their invite.
principles.verifiedBody: Payslips, contracts, employer invites and applications make reviews verified, and verified reviews count more.
principles.factsBody: Were you paid on time? Was overtime paid? Did they reply to applicants? Clear answers help people decide.
principles.fairBody: Claiming is free, every employer can reply, and reviews can't be bought or removed – by anyone.

About.why1: Most job sites are built for office jobs and big brands. For hourly work, what matters is the specific location: the manager, the schedule, whether pay arrives on time.
About.why2: We want every shift worker to know before they go, and every good employer to get credit for it.

IndexPage.metaTitle: RateThatJob Index – your workplace score, anywhere
IndexPage.metaDescription: The RateThatJob Index shows what your people say about working for you: a score from the last 12 months of reviews, with pay and hours facts. Put it on your careers page, job ads and email signature.
IndexPage.title: Happy people are the best job ad.
IndexPage.intro: The RateThatJob Index is your workplace score, built from what the people who work for you say. When a candidate sees a high Index, they know they'll be treated well – and can come to work with peace of mind.
IndexPage.exampleNote: These badges use made-up sample data. Yours show your real score and update on their own.
IndexPage.messageTitle: Trust you can't buy – only earn.
IndexPage.message1: Every job ad promises a great team and fair pay. The Index shows whether it's true: it comes from reviews by people who work or worked there, and from facts like whether pay arrives on time.
IndexPage.message2: That's why a high Index works harder than any slogan. It tells candidates that people here are paid, respected and listened to – and the only way to earn it is to be a good place to work.
IndexPage.whatBody: The Index is the overall score of a workplace on RateThatJob, from 1 to 5. Every location has its own. You can show it anywhere, and it always links back to your public profile, where candidates can read the reviews behind it.

how.windowBody: Only reviews published in the last 12 months count, so the score shows what it's like to work there now – not years ago.
how.categoriesBody: Next to the overall score, reviewers rate management, pay, schedule and work environment from 1 to 5.
how.factsBody: Yes/no answers turned into percentages: paid on time, paid as promised, overtime paid, the promised hours – and whether the employer replies to applicants.
how.verifiedBody: Reviews verified by a document, an employer invite or an application on RateThatJob count fully; unverified ones count half.
how.thresholdBody: The score appears once a location has 5 published reviews. Until then the badge invites people to rate you.

IndexPage.placesIntro: Your Index updates on its own. Every version links back to your public profile.

places.imageBody: A simple image with a link. Works on careers pages, in website builders and anywhere images and links are allowed.
places.widgetBody: One script for a live card on your site, light or dark, in English or Hungarian.
places.jsonBody: Your score, counts and facts as open JSON, for developers who want their own design.
places.emailBody: Add the image badge to your email signature, so every email shows how your people rate you.

IndexPage.improveTitle: What moves it – and how to raise it
IndexPage.improveIntro: The only way up is to be a better place to work, and to show it:

improve.reply: Reply to reviews openly, in any language.
improve.applicants: Reply to every applicant. Every decision or message counts as a reply in your ghosting meter.
improve.invite: Invite your team to rate you with your invite link. Invited reviews count as verified.
improve.pay: Pay on time and as promised, overtime included.
improve.hours: Give people the hours you promised.
improve.listen: Act on what reviews say about managers, schedules and the environment.

IndexPage.cannotBody: Employers can't delete reviews, and a better score can't be bought. You can dispute a review that isn't verified; our moderators decide.
IndexPage.warningBody: With Pro, your dashboard warns you when management, pay, schedule or environment drops by 0.5 or more in the last 60 days compared with before (with at least 5 reviews in both periods). So you notice a souring mood before it pulls your Index down.
IndexPage.sealBody: A location earns the seal with an Index of 4.0 or higher and at least 10 verified reviews in the last 12 months. The seal shows the current year and disappears if the location no longer qualifies.
IndexPage.topBody: An Index above 4.8 means that over a whole year nearly everyone who worked there gave top marks. Very few workplaces get there. If yours does, it's the strongest recruiting message you can have.

faq.whatA: The overall score of a workplace on RateThatJob, from 1 to 5, based on reviews from the last 12 months. Verified reviews count fully, unverified ones half.
faq.updateA: Yes. The badges, the widget and the JSON always show the current score. You never have to change the code.
faq.removeA: No. Employers can't delete or edit reviews, and scores can't be bought. You can reply publicly, and dispute a review that isn't verified – our moderators decide.
faq.fewQ: What if we have fewer than 5 reviews?
faq.fewA: The badge says "Rate us on RateThatJob" and links to the review form for your location. Share your invite link with your team to get there.
faq.costA: The Index for your website is part of Pro. Every location gets 30 days free with no card, starting when your claim is approved. After that Pro is billed per location; without it, your embedded badges stay but say the Index is currently unavailable. Your public profile and reviews are always visible.

CareersHub.applyIntro: The Apply button opens the job on RateThatJob in a new tab. Everything after that happens there:

apply.quickBody: No CV: candidates answer your yes/no questions in about a minute. Or ask for a CV if you prefer.
apply.aiBody: With the Basic and Pro packages, AI summarises every candidate for you; with Pro it also asks applicants a few follow-up questions. A person always decides.
apply.contactBody: Call candidates from the list or message them. They get it in their account, and by email if they gave one.
apply.backBody: After applying, candidates get a button back to the page they came from.

CareersHub.pricingLink: See job ad packages and prices

faq.costA: No. Careers Hub is free for every employer who has claimed their workplace, with or without Pro. Job ads are priced per ad – see Pricing.
faq.whereA: On any website where you can add HTML: your careers page, website builders that allow custom code, landing pages.
faq.noJobsQ: What if we have no open jobs?
faq.noJobsA: Careers Hub says there are no open jobs right now and still shows your RateThatJob Index.
faq.indexA: No. The RateThatJob Index is always shown under the jobs in Careers Hub. With Pro or the free trial it shows your score; otherwise it says the Index is currently unavailable.
faq.dataA: No cookies. We only record which websites show Careers Hub (the domain), so you can see where you're embedded.

CareersHub.bottomTitle: Put your jobs where your candidates already look.
CareersHub.bottomBody: Claim your workplace for free, post a job and copy your Careers Hub code from your dashboard.
